non_blocking_findings.title: Recorded-only evidence code can still turn a correct session into a miss if it raises
evidence: harness.py:389-394 runs proxy.match and recorded() (model_adapter.reported_models) inside cleanup(); cleanup appends 'cleanup record reconciliation: <Error>' to meta['failures'] (harness.py:338-342)
publish.py:196-198 and protected_regrade.py:23-24 count a session only when failures == []
Plan KTD5 (plan line 185) and R4/R5 say these fields never enter failures or the verdict
model_adapter.py:141, 168-171 and 204 assume dict events and integer usage values, so a null usage field or a non-object SSE payload would raise TypeError or AttributeError
non_blocking_findings.assessment: Latent: the frozen client versions produced well-formed output across the rehearsal and earlier development sessions. If a scored session misses only for this reason, the run record must name it as a harness-reason miss under R8. Do not repair it mid-experiment.

non_blocking_findings.title: Publication counts the independent regrade and never compares it with the live verdict
evidence: publish.py:195 takes row dimensions from protected_regrade only; the live meta['dimensions'] are validated for shape (publish.py:176-179) but never compared
harness.py:447-450 sets publication_integrity False, so every live manifest reads correct=false; both rehearsal manifests show this, which is by design

The regrade depends on retention: replay_bundle.py:11 (MAX_FILES 4096) and pinned.py:31 (regular files only) mean an agent work tree with more than about 4,000 files, or with a FIFO or socket, loses 'candidate' retention, and the regrade then fails source_tests and activation_identity although the live grade passed
non_blocking_findings.action: In PR2, publish each slot's live and regrade dimensions side by side and name any disagreement. Low probability; the rehearsal regrade matched the live grade exactly.
